The composite score is reported on the 1–5 scale. Free-response questions reward clear setup and justification, not just the final number — show the integral or derivative you evaluate.
MCQ: 45 points raw (1 pt each, no penalty). FRQ: 54 points (6 problems × 9 pts). Total 99 pts scaled to 1–5. Score of 3+ is generally considered passing.

label.en: ⚠ Critical College Board exam rules & timing traps

body.en:
The 3-decimal rounding rule: Any numerical answer derived on calculator-active sections (Section I Part B and Section II Part A) must be reported to at least 3 places after the decimal point (rounded or truncated). Never round intermediate values during your calculations!

Setup is required on FRQs: Writing down only a numerical answer obtained from your calculator with no calculus setup earns zero credit. Always write the definite integral, derivative equation, or limit before reporting the calculator's result.

Strict calculator containment: In Section II Part B (the final 60 minutes), you must put your graphing calculator away. You may continue working on or checking Questions 1 and 2, but without the calculator.

label.en: Exam strategy — Pacing & maximizing partial credit

body.en:
Pacing target: Budget approximately 2 minutes per multiple-choice question in Part A (60 min / 30 Q) and 3 minutes per question in Part B (45 min / 15 Q). On Section II, spend approximately 15 minutes per Free Response Question.

Harvesting independent points: If part (b) of an FRQ asks you to use the answer from part (a), but you were unable to solve (a), clearly state an assumed value or symbolic representation for (a) and carry out the correct calculus method in (b). AP readers award full follow-through points for correct logic!

question.en: In Section I Part A of the AP Calculus AB exam, students must complete 30 non-calculator multiple-choice questions in 60 minutes. If a student spends 90 seconds on average on each of the first 20 questions, how many minutes remain on average for each of the final 10 questions?

solution.en:
Step 1: Calculate total time available in seconds: \[ 60\text{ minutes} \times 60\text{ seconds/minute} = 3600\text{ seconds}. \]

Step 2: Calculate time spent on the first 20 questions: \[ 20 \times 90\text{ seconds} = 1800\text{ seconds (30 minutes)}. \]

Step 3: Calculate remaining time: \[ 3600 - 1800 = 1800\text{ seconds (30 minutes)}. \]

Step 4: Calculate average time per remaining question: \[ \frac{1800\text{ seconds}}{10\text{ questions}} = 180\text{ seconds} = 3.0\text{ minutes per question}. \]

question.en: Section II Part A consists of 2 free-response questions in 30 minutes where a graphing calculator is required. A student uses numerical integration (fnInt) to evaluate \(\int_1^4 \sqrt{x^3 + 2}\,dx\). The calculator displays \(12.784619\). According to College Board AP scoring conventions, what acceptable rounded or truncated value should the student report, and what setup must be written in the exam booklet?

solution.en:
Step 1: State the required mathematical setup: Writing only the numeric result earns 0 points. The student must write the definite integral: \[ \int_1^4 \sqrt{x^3 + 2}\,dx. \]

Step 2: Apply the 3-decimal rule: AP guidelines accept answers rounded or truncated to 3 decimal places:

  • Truncated: \(12.784\)
  • Rounded: \(12.785\)

Both \(12.784\) and \(12.785\) receive full credit.
